clue.text: Part of wimple — a thermal material

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nun's headdress with a warm lining, described by the fabric it is made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleather is plastic imitation leather, a fabric, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Literary alter ego in cloak, say

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word as it is spoken, keeping its sound but not its spelling

parts.note: to cloak something is to hide it

explanation.surface: A character from fiction lurks inside a disguising cloak, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Hyde is the evil other self of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's novella; 'say' signals that HIDE is heard, not written.
explanation.definitionFit: In Stevenson's story Hyde is the second personality Jekyll turns into, a classic fictional alter ego.

clue.text: Eccentric imprisons neighbourhood extremists in capital

indicators.note: imprisons means one piece locks the other up inside it

parts.note: a loon is an eccentric or crazy person

indicators.note: extremists here means the outermost letters of the word neighbourhood

explanation.surface: A local oddball holds the area's radicals captive in a major city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' looks like political radicals but only wants the end letters of the next word; 'imprisons' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital city of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Study with pen restrains one's stupidity

parts.note: a den is a private study or room for working in

indicators.note: restrains means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
one's read as 'one is' gives the Roman numeral I for one

explanation.surface: Someone working with a pen is held back by their own foolishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' reads as a writing tool but is an animal enclosure; 'restrains' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Density can mean thickness of mind, slowness to understand, which is stupidity.

clue.text: Most costly sword picked up between two streets

indicators.note: between means the piece sits in the middle of the other letters
two asks for the abbreviation for street to be written twice

parts.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for street

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the word is read upwards, so it runs backwards

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: The priciest blade is collected somewhere between two roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests lifting, but in a down light it means read upwards; 'two' doubles the street abbreviation and 'between' places the sword in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is an informal word for expensive, so steepest is priciest.

clue.text: Work very hard to forge two blades — takes love

indicators.note: to forge is to hammer metal into a new shape, so these letters are beaten into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, giving O

explanation.surface: A smith toils to make a pair of swords, taking much affection to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to forge' rearranges TWO BLADES together with O for love, which 'takes' adds to the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat blood is an idiom for labouring or striving with great effort.

clue.text: Newly-wed receives £1,000 cross

indicators.note: receives means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a bride is a woman newly wed
a grand is a thousand pounds, abbreviated G

explanation.surface: A newly married woman is given a thousand pounds and is angry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is the verb to cross, as a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge a gap or river is to span or go across it.

clue.text: Master follows amateur into interior with weapon

indicators.note: into means the pieces are put inside the word for interior

parts.note: the core is the inner part of something

indicators.note: follows means the abbreviation for master comes after the word for amateur

parts.note: lay means non-professional, amateur
M is an abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree

explanation.surface: An expert trails a novice into the heart of the country, carrying arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large Scottish two-edged broadsword, so a weapon.

clue.text: Wrote about in column

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of wrote are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journalist wrote a piece about something in their newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' hints at journalism but means a tall structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower is a tall narrow structure, like a column or pillar.

clue.text: Tense worried comedian

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
something that ate at you worried you

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic is nervous and anxious before a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Tate is a British comic actress known for her sketch show.

clue.text: Ignores dried grass being threshed

indicators.note: threshing beats grain loose, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Hay is beaten on a farm while someone pays it no attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to pay no heed to it, to overlook it.

clue.text: Barman: c-climb aboard

parts.note: the stammered letter c is taken as written
to hop in is to climb aboard a vehicle

explanation.surface: A stuttering pub worker invites someone to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' suggests a pub but means a man of musical bars, a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin wrote music measured in bars, so he is jokingly a man of bars.

clue.text: Motor enthusiast modifies other pedal

indicators.note: modifies means the letters are altered into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A car fan tinkers with a second pedal on their vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrolhead is slang for someone obsessed with cars and motor sport.

clue.text: Prince blows top over catching maiden with Edward and shook

indicators.note: catching means the first piece traps the next one inside it
over tells us the word that is left is turned back to front
blows top says the prince's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Albert was Queen Victoria's husband, the Prince Consort
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A royal loses his temper after seizing a young woman, with Edward shaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows top' leaves LBERT, which 'over' turns to TREBL before 'catching' takes in the maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble is to quiver or shake, so trembled is shook in the past tense.

clue.text: National fractured his rib touring Thailand

indicators.note: touring means the broken letters go around the abbreviation for Thailand
fractured means the letters are broken and put back in a new order

parts.note: T is the international vehicle registration for Thailand

explanation.surface: A tourist breaks a bone while travelling in Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fractured' turns HIS RIB into BRIISH, and 'touring' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: British is the nationality adjective for the United Kingdom, a national label.

clue.text: Moving without control, starting to stretch then pulling leg

indicators.note: starting to points to the opening letter of the word stretch

parts.note: pulling someone's leg means teasing or kidding them

explanation.surface: A sportsman begins warming up, then strains a leg muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulling leg' suggests an injury but means joking.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle skidding slides on the road surface with the driver unable to steer.

clue.text: Bad tempered mole left to retire indoors

indicators.note: indoors means a piece is placed inside the word for mole

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted in an organisation

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word for left is read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A grumpy undercover agent leaves to settle down in retirement at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' and 'indoors' read like a pensioner's life but signal a reversal and an insertion; 'mole' is the secret agent, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroppy is British slang for irritable and argumentative, bad tempered.

clue.text: Following criminal turns up around Australia

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go about the abbreviation for Australia
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: A is the vehicle registration letter for Australia

explanation.surface: An offender reappears somewhere near Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges TURNS UP into PURSUNT, and 'around' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuant, as in pursuant to, means in accordance with or following on from.

clue.text: Sun hack is not to remove the halo

indicators.note: hack means chop up, so the letters of sun are cut and rearranged

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial contraction of is not

explanation.surface: A tabloid reporter from The Sun refuses to tarnish a celebrity's virtuous image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a journalist but tells us to rearrange SUN into UNS. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is pictured with a halo, so to unsaint someone is to strip that holy status.

clue.text: Perhaps Boris Johnson welcomes special European

indicators.note: welcomes means the first piece takes the second into it

parts.note: Boris Johnson went to Eton College, so he is an example of an Etonian

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister greets a distinguished visitor from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite English boarding school; 'Perhaps' marks Boris Johnson as one example of its old boys.
explanation.definitionFit: An Estonian comes from Estonia, a Baltic country in Europe.

clue.text: Difficult to break into small, small pieces

indicators.note: to break into means one piece forces its way inside the others

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
S again stands for small
something hard is difficult

explanation.surface: It is hard to smash something into tiny fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Shards are sharp broken fragments, such as of glass or pottery.

clue.text: New demo broken up by force

indicators.note: broken up means the letters of demo are smashed into a new order

parts.note: the RN, the Royal Navy, is an armed force

explanation.surface: A fresh protest march is dispersed by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken up' signals the anagram; 'force' is the Royal Navy, not the police the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date or recent, the opposite of old.

clue.text: Think outside of uniform heritage centre

parts.note: to muse is to think or ponder

indicators.note: outside of points to the first and last letters of uniform

explanation.surface: Consider what lies beyond conformity at a historic visitor attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A museum keeps and displays historical artefacts, a place for preserving a country's past.

clue.text: Ground had scarlet buildings

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are pounded into a new order

explanation.surface: A patch of land was covered in red structures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun for land but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathedrals are large churches, a kind of building.

clue.text: Boy's father has regular build

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: regular picks out every other letter of the word build

explanation.surface: A son's dad has an average physique.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul is a common male given name, so it can stand for a boy.

clue.text: Outdoor area, one surrounded by three men?

indicators.note: surrounded by means the letter for one sits inside the other letters

parts.note: in chess the pieces are called men; P, R and K are pawn, rook and king
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A lone figure in open space is hemmed in by a trio of blokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the 'men' are chessmen, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: A park is a public green space in a town, an outdoor area.

clue.text: Illustrated in Crimean War during revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the run of letters is read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Pictured at the time of the Crimean War, during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds NWARD inside 'Crimean War during', and 'revolution' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn means sketched or depicted in pictures, so illustrated.

clue.text: Urine not flowing? It's definitely not a big thing!

definitions.text: It's definitely not a big thing!

indicators.note: flowing means the letters run freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A problem passing water is played down as nothing serious.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a neutrino is a subatomic particle, about as small as a thing gets.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is a tiny, nearly massless subatomic particle, so hardly a big object.
